workPackages.title: Approve the Cotsel release scope and authority baseline
workPackages.objective: Freeze the pilot mode, value limits, user roles, cross-repository commits, contract economics, cloud owner, data classes, provider boundaries, risk acceptance, and RACI.
workPackages.inScope: The release charter; system-of-record boundaries; pilot mode, participants, jurisdictions, values and limits; cross-repository and contract identities; cloud and provider ownership; data classes; risk acceptance; RACI; blocker register; release manifest; evidence index; golden-journey definitions; and dependency-based forecast.
workPackages.outOfScope: Protocol, service, database, infrastructure, observability, assurance, pilot-operation, and mainnet implementation owned by WP-1 through WP-12. WP-0 records and approves those boundaries but does not implement them.
workPackages.reviewers: Product authority, Finance authority, Engineering Lead, and affected service owners
workPackages.dependencies: None. Named authorities and account or provider inventories are prerequisites for acceptance.
workPackages.implementation: Approve the release charter, system-of-record matrix, blocker register, manifest and evidence schemas, ownership, change and defect controls, seven journeys, and dependency-based forecast.
workPackages.verification: Review every authority boundary, assumption, exclusion, environment, decision, owner, dependency, and change invalidation rule for completeness and internal consistency.
workPackages.evidence: Approved release charter, system-of-record matrix, blocker register, release-manifest schema, evidence-index schema, responsibility register, decision log, and dependency-based forecast.
workPackages.rollback: Stop all downstream acceptance when scope, owner, provider, cloud, value, participant, or authority is ambiguous. Reopen affected work and gates after any material change.
workPackages.residualRisk: Business, legal, financial, provider, and authority decisions remain open until named decision-makers accept them. No technical issue may invent them.
workPackages.milestone: M0 Base Migration Decision and Boundary Freeze

workPackages.title: Correct the protocol and deploy the current contract
workPackages.objective: Establish buyer-authorized inspection acceptance, recoverable governance, role separation, mandatory verification, and one current Base Sepolia contract.
workPackages.inScope: AgroasysEscrow source, ABI and deployment tooling; buyer-signed inspection acceptance; administrator rotation, quorum, epoch and unpause controls; protocol role separation; contract test suites; source, bytecode, role and address verification; Base Sepolia redeployment; consumer address propagation; and contract-cohort rollback.
workPackages.outOfScope: Gateway broadcast durability, indexer reconstruction, treasury provider completion, cloud provisioning, controlled-pilot operation, and Base mainnet authorization except where WP-1 supplies an explicit dependency or evidence input.
workPackages.reviewers: Security authority, Release Owner, Gateway Owner, Oracle Owner, and Finance authority
workPackages.implementation: Implement buyer signatures, administrator removal and replacement, quorum and epoch controls, safe unpause, role separation, canonical deployment, live bytecode comparison, and cohort rollback.
workPackages.verification: Run Hardhat, Foundry, fuzz, invariant, static, deployment, role, negative-signature, governance-rotation, and cohort-rollback tests on the pinned source.
workPackages.evidence: Independent contract review, clean required contract suites, explorer-verified current deployment, live role and bytecode attestation, address propagation, and rollback evidence.
workPackages.rollback: Stop new intake and retain the previous cohort only when compatibility and exposure are known. Pause affected actions on any address, role, ABI, or governance mismatch.
workPackages.residualRisk: A non-upgradeable contract cannot move active funds automatically. Cohort and reconciliation controls must bound that risk.
workPackages.milestone: M1 Base Contract Runtime and Deployment

workPackages.title: Make transaction intent and outcome handling durable
workPackages.objective: Guarantee one authoritative outcome for every financial command across signing, broadcast, confirmation, timeout, restart, callback, and custody modes.
workPackages.inScope: Gateway and Oracle command intake; canonical intent and signer-response comparison; durable reservation, queue, outbox and lease behavior; broadcast-before-wait persistence; unknown-outcome recovery; nonce, receipt and event resolution; callback authentication and replay protection; finality policy; idempotency retention; monetary ingress; and approved signer custody modes.
workPackages.outOfScope: Contract authorization design owned by WP-1, complete indexer and reconciliation coverage owned by WP-3, treasury close owned by WP-4, and cloud resource provisioning owned by WP-7.
workPackages.reviewers: Oracle Owner, Platform Owner, Security authority, Finance authority, and Reconciliation Owner
workPackages.dependencies: WP-0 and the WP-1 contract interface
workPackages.implementation: Add canonical signer comparison, broadcast-before-wait persistence, explicit unknown states, nonce and receipt recovery, durable queues and callback leases, exact-byte HMAC, unified finality, idempotency retention, and fail-closed signer custody.
workPackages.verification: Inject termination, timeout, signer mutation, RPC split, nonce conflict, callback loss, replay, duplicate, redrive, custody outage, and amount-boundary failures for every financial action class.
workPackages.evidence: A crash and timeout matrix proves one authoritative outcome without rebroadcast under raw test custody and approved KMS or MPC custody modes.
workPackages.rollback: Pause new commands when any accepted broadcast is untracked. Resolve receipt, event, nonce, and contract state before retry or resumption.
workPackages.residualRisk: Providers and the network can remain temporarily ambiguous. The system must preserve and own that ambiguity rather than infer failure or success.
workPackages.milestone: M2 Base Eventing, Reconciliation, and Treasury Safety

workPackages.title: Make indexer and reconciliation coverage complete
workPackages.objective: Process every canonical event exactly once or quarantine it visibly, and reconcile chain and projection state in both directions across the complete range.
workPackages.inScope: Indexer ABI, code and chain preflight; poison-log quarantine; atomic checkpoints; canonical chain-derived coverage; bidirectional reconciliation; keyset cursors; block-bounded reports; replay and redrive; lease recovery; missing and extra record detection; reorganization handling inputs; and capacity beyond 1,000 trades.
workPackages.outOfScope: Protocol changes owned by WP-1, transaction dispatch owned by WP-2, treasury state transitions owned by WP-4, and infrastructure provisioning owned by WP-7 except for required interfaces and evidence.
workPackages.reviewers: Reconciliation Owner, Data Owner, Treasury Owner, Protocol Owner, and Operations Lead
workPackages.implementation: Add poison-log quarantine, atomic checkpoints, chain and ABI preflight, chain-derived coverage, keyset cursors, block-bounded reports, lease recovery, deterministic replay, and capacity beyond 1,000 trades.
workPackages.verification: Test malformed logs, missing parents, ABI drift, reorg, chain-only and indexer-only records, stale checkpoints, sole-RPC failure, abandoned runs, replay, and large coverage sets.
workPackages.evidence: Complete coverage reports, deterministic replay hashes, alert and redrive records, exact block and trade ranges, and unresolved-drift ownership.
workPackages.rollback: Stop checkpoints on poison evidence and freeze affected financial progression until replay and downstream reconciliation complete.
workPackages.residualRisk: Chain and provider finality may disagree temporarily. Reports must expose the exact bounded state and prevent false clean results.
workPackages.milestone: M2 Base Eventing, Reconciliation, and Treasury Safety

workPackages.title: Make treasury and external handoff state authoritative
workPackages.objective: Permit accrual, eligibility, export, handoff, realization, and close only from finalized canonical evidence, fresh reconciliation, authenticated actors, and authoritative provider completion.
workPackages.inScope: Finalized canonical fee ingestion; reorganization rollback; autonomous freshness-gated ingestion; append-only provider and handoff states; verified callbacks; atomic maker-checker transitions; authenticated actor identity; canonical monetary values; complete exports; discrepancy freeze; provider confirmation; reconciliation clearance; realization; and close evidence.
workPackages.outOfScope: External bank or provider operation, legal classification, contract event production, and participant-ledger ownership. Those authorities supply evidence but cannot be replaced by a Cotsel request or local state.
workPackages.reviewers: Finance authority, Data Owner, Reconciliation Owner, Security authority, and external-provider owner
workPackages.implementation: Add finalized canonical ingestion, reorg rollback, autonomous freshness-gated workers, append-only provider states, atomic maker-checker transitions, authenticated actors, canonical money, complete exports, and reconciliation-gated realization.
workPackages.verification: Test reorgs, stopped ingestion, CREATED and FAILED provider states, conflicting callbacks, concurrent transitions, actor mismatch, noncanonical money, stale reconciliation, truncation, and provider timeout.
workPackages.evidence: End-to-end fee accrual, claim, handoff, provider confirmation, discrepancy handling, reconciliation, and close records with no false completion.
workPackages.rollback: Freeze affected batches, preserve conflicting evidence, revoke orphan eligibility, and resume only after approved correction and fresh reconciliation.
workPackages.residualRisk: External provider and bank completion remains outside Cotsel authority and requires independently verifiable evidence.
workPackages.milestone: M2 Base Eventing, Reconciliation, and Treasury Safety

workPackages.title: Make data migration and recovery production-safe
workPackages.objective: Move schema authority out of runtime services and restore all seven databases, roles, RLS, configuration, indexer state, and financial truth within approved objectives.
workPackages.inScope: All seven Cotsel databases; versioned migration jobs and identities; expand, backfill and contract sequencing; advisory locking; runtime-DDL denial; least-privilege roles and RLS; encrypted backup and PITR; immutable retention; restoration order; clean-environment restore; re-indexing; ledger, chain and treasury reconciliation; and measured RPO and RTO.
workPackages.outOfScope: Application feature changes unrelated to schema compatibility, provider-owned data recovery, and any financial resumption before WP-3 and WP-4 reconciliation evidence is accepted.
workPackages.reviewers: Data Owner, affected Service Owners, Security authority, Reconciliation Owner, and Finance authority
workPackages.implementation: Create versioned migration jobs, expand and backfill and contract compatibility, least-privilege roles, encrypted backup and PITR, immutable retention, restoration order, re-index rules, and ledger and chain reconciliation.
workPackages.verification: Run production-size migration, concurrent-start, partial-failure, runtime-DDL denial, rollback compatibility, clean restore, grants, RLS, idempotency, re-index, and financial tie-out tests.
workPackages.evidence: Migration ledger, applied identity, restore manifest, row and hash checks, grant and RLS proof, service readiness, re-index results, tie-out, and measured RPO and RTO.
workPackages.rollback: Stop rollout on migration error and use only proven compatible rollback or roll-forward. Block financial resumption until recovery and reconciliation pass.
workPackages.residualRisk: Schema and application compatibility is time-bounded. Each release must record its exact safe rollback window.

workPackages.title: Build an immutable and truthful release supply chain
workPackages.objective: Build every service once from clean source and block promotion unless every required code, contract, data, image, security, recovery, and integration check is complete.
workPackages.inScope: Cotsel build contexts and service images; non-root runtime hardening; pinned actions, images and dependencies; lint, type, test, contract, migration, security and integration aggregation; SAST, secret, dependency, license, container and IaC scanning; SBOM, provenance and signing; protected paths and environments; promotion policy; active runbooks; and compatible rollback artifacts.
workPackages.outOfScope: Provisioning the target cloud resources owned by WP-7, accepting independent assurance owned by WP-10, and creating permanent gate-review issues without a real release candidate.
workPackages.reviewers: Platform Owner, Security authority, Protocol Owner, Data Owner, and Integration Lead
workPackages.implementation: Repair image contexts, create non-root images, pin inputs, scan, generate SBOM and provenance, sign digests, complete the aggregate, route shared packages, protect sensitive paths, and correct active runbooks.
workPackages.verification: Use clean-cache image builds, runtime probes, seeded scanner failures, aggregate meta-tests, shared-consumer mutations, required review tests, emergency-bypass audit, and command and link validation.
workPackages.evidence: Signed digest manifest, SBOM, scan and provenance reports, complete hosted gates, protected review records, and tested deployment and rollback instructions.
workPackages.rollback: Do not promote an unverified artifact. Revoke compromised artifacts and credentials and deploy only a previously accepted compatible digest.
workPackages.residualRisk: Third-party actions, packages, and images can change or be compromised. Immutable pinning and recurring review must remain active.

workPackages.title: Provision the production-like cloud and network path
workPackages.objective: Run Cotsel in one approved cloud control plane with reviewed IaC, private networking, managed HA dependencies, protected deployment, deterministic configuration, and safe readiness.
workPackages.inScope: The approved production-like staging cloud; reviewed IaC and protected apply; private network and origin denial; approved edge, TLS, WAF and rate controls; immutable compute; managed HA PostgreSQL and Redis, and durable queues; primary and fallback RPC; managed secrets and signer identities; deterministic configuration; dependency-aware readiness; capacity; safe deployment; and rollback.
workPackages.outOfScope: Frontend, backend and dashboard repository implementation; provider operation outside the approved cloud boundary; controlled-pilot authorization; and Base mainnet resources before WP-12 approval.
workPackages.reviewers: Security authority, SRE Lead, Release Owner, Data Owner, and affected Service Owners
workPackages.implementation: Provision network, compute, managed database and cache, durable queues, TLS and WAF, origin denial, secrets and signer identities, RPC policy, config validation, capacity, readiness, deployment, and rollback.
workPackages.verification: Review plans and applies, scan external and internal ports, test origin denial, HA failover, dependency faults, wrong config, dead RPC, signer outage, capacity, safe rollout, and rollback.
workPackages.evidence: Reviewed IaC, protected apply, network and runtime identity, external scan, HA and load results, failure drill, config digest, deployment record, and rollback record.
workPackages.rollback: Remove traffic and pause new financial commitments on unsafe readiness, identity, dependency, capacity, or configuration state.
workPackages.residualRisk: Cloud and provider controls remain external evidence dependencies and cannot be accepted from repository configuration alone.

workPackages.title: Deploy observability, incident response, and evidence custody
workPackages.objective: Detect and route every critical financial or operational condition, correlate the complete journey, protect telemetry privacy, retain evidence, and rehearse containment and recovery.
workPackages.inScope: Central redacted logs, metrics and traces; end-to-end correlation; SLOs, settlement dashboards and synthetics; alert ownership, paging and escalation; durable notification evidence; privacy-safe schemas and retention; immutable evidence custody; corrected runbooks; and live drills for all failure-register cases, rollback, recovery, reconciliation and safe resumption.
workPackages.outOfScope: Using monitoring as settlement authority, accepting service or provider state without reconciliation, and closing implementation defects owned by WP-1 through WP-7 without their separate evidence.
workPackages.reviewers: Operations Lead, Incident Commander, Privacy authority, Security authority, and Finance authority
workPackages.dependencies: WP-2 through WP-7 telemetry and runtime
workPackages.implementation: Deploy redacted logs, metrics, traces, dashboards, SLOs, synthetics, on-call, durable notifications, immutable evidence storage, corrected runbooks, and incident, rollback, drift, signer, provider, and recovery drills.
workPackages.verification: Inject every failure-register case, verify page and escalation, trace correlation, privacy redaction, evidence retrieval, pause and freeze, rollback, recovery, reconciliation, and safe resumption.
workPackages.evidence: Dashboards, alerts, receipts, owner roster, traces, redaction reports, signed drill records, runbooks, retained evidence index, response times, and follow-up defects.
workPackages.rollback: Freeze risky flows when an alert is unowned, evidence cannot be retained, or recovery cannot prove financial reconciliation.
workPackages.residualRisk: Monitoring is not settlement authority. Service, chain, ledger, and provider truth must remain independently reconciled.

workPackages.title: Prove cross-repository contracts and user journeys
workPackages.objective: Pin and verify Agroasys backend, platform.v1, Cotsel-Dash, Cotsel, contract, chain, and provider behavior through hosted end-to-end journeys.
workPackages.inScope: The pinned Agroasys backend, platform.v1, Cotsel-Dash and Cotsel identities; contract, ABI, chain and provider modes; hosted compatibility; Cotsel session exchange and refresh; privileged exchange; Ricardian retrieval; buyer, supplier, operator and support journeys; funding, release, inspection, treasury, reconciliation, recovery and incident behavior; and browser-to-chain evidence.
workPackages.outOfScope: Unpinned local-only paths, mock-only financial proof, implementation changes in external repositories under this Cotsel-only programme, and self-acceptance of evidence owned by another repository or provider.
workPackages.reviewers: Product QA Lead, Agroasys backend owner, platform.v1 owner, Cotsel-Dash owner, Protocol Owner, and Operations Lead
workPackages.implementation: Repair and require M3, harden Cotsel sessions and privileged exchange, authorize Ricardian retrieval, and implement deployed login, funding, release, inspection, treasury, reconciliation, recovery, incident, and support journeys.
workPackages.verification: Run hosted compatibility plus all seven golden journeys and every disabled-user, role-drift, replay, wrong-wallet, timeout, reorg, forged acceptance, provider failure, restore, and incident variant.
workPackages.evidence: Pinned manifest, hosted compatibility matrix, browser and operator records, chain receipts, callbacks, ledger effects, reconciliation, support evidence, and accepted failure results.
workPackages.rollback: Show pending or failed truth, pause new progression, and use controlled recovery. Never infer success from browser, dashboard, gateway, indexer, or provider-request state alone.
workPackages.residualRisk: Other repositories and external providers must supply their own evidence. Cotsel cannot self-accept their authority.
workPackages.milestone: M3 Backend, Gateway, and Wallet Continuity

workPackages.title: Complete security, compliance, privacy, and independent assurance
workPackages.objective: Approve and test the complete control boundary and obtain independent assurance for the stable contract, application, cloud, signer, provider, privacy, and financial workflow.
workPackages.inScope: Threat and abuse analysis; independent contract, API, application, cloud and financial-workflow testing; identity and compliance authority; participant and provider due diligence evidence; data inventory and classification; privacy rights; telemetry privacy; financial controls; retention, legal hold and destruction; incident and breach decisions; safe errors; remediation verification; and required legal and financial approvals.
workPackages.outOfScope: Providing legal advice, regulatory classification, financial-statement audit or certification, and accepting unresolved Critical or High findings or blank legal, compliance, privacy, finance or provider decisions.
workPackages.reviewers: Compliance authority, Privacy authority, Finance authority, legal counsel, Protocol Owner, Platform Owner, and independent assessor
workPackages.dependencies: A stable WP-1 through WP-9 candidate
workPackages.implementation: Complete threat and abuse review, independent contract and application and cloud tests, data and privacy governance, KYB and KYT and sanctions boundary, provider assurance, retention, evidence custody, safe errors, and legal and financial approvals.
workPackages.verification: Test authorization, isolation, ingress, signer, provider, secrets, telemetry, privacy rights, retention, breach, maker-checker, discrepancy freeze, and every independent finding remediation.
workPackages.evidence: Remediation-verified independent reports, approved data and provider controls, signed legal and financial decisions, retention proof, and no unaccepted critical or high finding.
workPackages.rollback: Block pilot or mainnet on any unresolved control decision, unaccepted critical or high finding, evidence-custody failure, or provider-authority ambiguity.
workPackages.residualRisk: The SOW is not legal advice or certification. Named legal, compliance, finance, and security authorities retain the decisions.

workPackages.title: Authorize and operate the controlled pilot
workPackages.objective: Run only the approved candidate for named trained participants within fixed value and volume caps, staffed support, live monitoring, daily reconciliation, and tested stop conditions.
workPackages.inScope: Named participant allowlist and eligibility; consent and training; approved jurisdiction, value and volume caps; staffed support and incident contacts; the exact release window and manifest; zero-value and bounded-value rehearsal; all seven golden journeys; live monitoring; daily reconciliation and incident summaries; stop authority; evidence archive; closeout; and separately approved expansion decisions.
workPackages.outOfScope: Public registration, unknown participants, uncapped or unsupported value, unsupported jurisdictions, Base mainnet, automatic expansion, and operation while any applicable E or P gate, evidence field, alert owner, restore proof or discrepancy remains unresolved.
workPackages.reviewers: Operations Lead, Product authority, Compliance authority, Finance authority, Engineering Lead, Treasury Owner, and Incident Commander
workPackages.dependencies: All applicable E-0 through E-5 and P-0 through P-6 gates
workPackages.implementation: Approve participants, consent, training, caps, support, and stop authority; run zero-value and bounded-value rehearsal; monitor live operation; reconcile daily; retain evidence; close incidents; and record GO, closeout, and expansion decisions.
workPackages.verification: Exercise all golden journeys, support, pause, freeze, incident, rollback, recovery, and daily reconciliation within the exact release and window.
workPackages.evidence: Signed GO, exact manifest, participant and limit record, fresh retrievable evidence packet, bounded pilot results, daily reconciliation, incident closeout, and explicit expansion decision.
workPackages.rollback: Stop immediately on unknown participant, uncapped value, unsupported jurisdiction, unowned alert, failed restore, unresolved drift, evidence gap, or expired exception.
workPackages.residualRisk: Pilot authorization is bounded and temporary. Expansion requires new evidence and approval.

workPackages.title: Authorize Base mainnet as a separate change programme
workPackages.objective: Authorize mainnet only after a successful controlled pilot and separate proof of contract, application, treasury, signer, provider, capacity, assurance, canary, rollback, and four-role approval.
workPackages.inScope: A separate mainnet change record; verified mainnet contract, source, bytecode, roles, ABI, address, USDC and chain; protected application release; production IaC, signer and provider capacity; treasury and off-ramp controls; daily reconciliation; exposure freeze; first-cohort canary; live-money incident and rollback drills; independent assurance; and explicit four-role GO.
workPackages.outOfScope: Automatic promotion from Base Sepolia, reuse of pilot evidence without documented equivalence, broad rollout beyond the approved first cohort, and mainnet activity before the separate deployment, provider, assurance, rollback and four-role conditions are accepted.
workPackages.reviewers: Engineering Lead, Operations Lead, Treasury Owner, Incident Commander, Security authority, and Compliance authority
workPackages.dependencies: Successful pilot and every mainnet condition
workPackages.implementation: Approve the mainnet change record, deploy and verify the mainnet contract and protected application, prove signer and provider capacity, treasury and off-ramp controls, cohort rollback, live-money drills, independent review, and explicit four-role GO.
workPackages.verification: Run mainnet-specific deployment, role, provider, capacity, load, failover, low-balance, signer outage, treasury, reconciliation, canary, pause, rollback, and incident tests.
workPackages.evidence: Explicit GO, verified mainnet deployment, signed application manifest, protected change record, independent assurance, monitored canary cohort, rollback, zero-drift reconciliation, and four-role approval.
workPackages.rollback: Pause new intake, freeze affected exposure, stop or roll back the canary cohort, reconcile all active contracts and providers, and resume only after new approval.
workPackages.residualRisk: A successful Base Sepolia pilot does not authorize mainnet. Every mainnet artifact, provider, limit, and approval must be fresh.
workPackages.milestone: M5 Base Mainnet Launch and Polkadot Retirement
